name: Walking to School in Xi'an: Children's Five Pairwise Questions
description:
Method replication: primary school children (grades 1–6) compare pairs of Xi'an street views on the five walking needs used in the paper (feasibility, accessibility, safety, comfort, pleasurability), 12 pairs each, 60 forced choices in all as in the paper, after answering how often and with whom they walk to school; the images are not the paper's stimuli (98 re-fetched Baidu street views of Xi'an's six core districts, 2019–2024, camera tilted slightly down towards a child's view).

Original study: Gao, Wang & Wang (2026), EPJ Data Science 15, 57. Pupils in grades 1–6 in Xi'an's six core urban districts completed, on tablets during a field survey (September–November 2024), a SurveyMonkey pairwise experiment with 240 Baidu street scenes (four directions per point, pitch adjusted to a child's eye level), making 60 forced choices across the five dimensions of Alfonzo's hierarchy of walking needs. Elo scores trained a CNN, and XGBoost–SHAP related perceived and built-environment factors to weekly walking frequency.

Differences from the original study: (1) newly fetched Baidu street views instead of the authors' 240 images, which are not released; (2) the paper gives only the definitions of the five dimensions, so the child-friendly question wording is written for this template and the definitions are shown under each question; (3) 12 pairs per dimension, since the paper does not report how the 60 choices were split; (4) background questions (grade, gender, walking days, companions) follow the paper's variables but are worded for this template.
author: Gao, Wang & Wang
